reviews.name: Mubeen Kamani
reviews.review_text: Alhamdulillah we had the chance to eat at The Chef Grill in Elk Grove Village and it was an amazing experience from start to finish. The restaurant serves fully halal food, which makes it a blessing to find such authentic Turkish and Mediterranean cuisine you can enjoy with peace of mind. The staff was friendly and welcoming, creating a warm atmosphere that instantly reminded me of the hospitality in Istanbul. The food was authentic, full of rich flavors, and beautifully presented. We started with the hot appetizer plate and every item on it was excellent. The falafel was flavorful and crispy even though I am usually not a fan. The kibbeh had the perfect texture with a savory filling, and there was a potato patty that was especially delicious. You could tell everything was freshly prepared with care. For the main dishes we tried the iskender kebab and the beyti kebab, and both were outstanding. The iskender kebab came with tender slices of halal meat served over pieces of bread, topped with a rich tomato sauce and a drizzle of melted butter with yogurt on the side. It truly brought back memories of meals in Istanbul. The beyti kebab was wrapped in lavash bread, covered with tomato sauce, and served with rice and grilled vegetables. It was rich, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned. The service throughout was excellent. The prices were on the higher side but the quality and authenticity of the food made it worth every dollar. Overall it was a wonderful halal dining experience and a place I would happily visit again inshaAllah. Food: 5 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 5 3-4 people

reviews.review_text: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (Easily a 10-star experience!) I visited The Chef, a Turkish cuisine restaurant, and it was absolutely brilliant from start to finish. I ordered the lentil soup, mozzarella sticks, and lamb chops, and every single dish was cooked to perfection. The flavors were rich, fresh, and exactly what you hope for when you walk into an authentic Turkish spot. What impressed me even more was the level of service—especially at 9 a.m. I honestly didn’t expect such high-quality food and attentive service that early in the morning, but they completely surprised me. Everything came out hot, delicious, and beautifully prepared. The lentil soup was comforting and full of flavor, the mozzarella sticks were perfectly crispy, and the lamb chops were tender and seasoned just right. You can tell the chefs take pride in what they serve. Overall, this place truly deserves 10 stars. Great food, excellent service, and an experience that exceeded my expectations. reviews.name: Nicholas P
reviews.review_text: Not many Turkish restaurants in the burbs. I went to Thousand Tales, that one was pretty solid but also very busy. Parking can be horrible on the weekend. This one is much more manageable, parking is way easier. At least you don’t have far to walk. We were a group of 4 and we just walked in without reservation. I recommend getting a reservation on the weekend. Middle Eastern people love getting dinner late, especially 7 PM to close. You’ll be surprised at how busy it still gets at like 9 PM and after. We ordered cig kofte, lamahcun, king chef mixed grill (4-5 ppl), pistachio and cheese kunefe, orange pistachio semolina with ice cream, and pistachio cheesecake. This is about 4.5 but I’ll round it to 5 here. Prices are competitive with Thousand Tales. Service is better here and much more attentive. -cig kofte 4 - this is a traditional Turkish cold dish. It has some spice. Good flavor. Make sure you squeeze some lemon onto it before eating. You eat it with lettuce. I didn’t love it but it was interesting to try. -lamahcun 5 - Turkish pizza. We got two pieces, 1 piece is big enough to split between two people. You add the ingredients to a piece, then roll it up like a burrito. That’s how you eat it. These are pretty good and a popular appetizer. -king chef mixed grill 5 - this has chicken shish, chicken adana, lamb shish, lamb adana, lamb chops, lamb shawarma, meatballs, beyti kebab, arugula salad, rice, bulgur, and French fries. French fries are really crispy. The rice and bulgur are delicious, you can taste the flavor. I like to eat the arugula salad on top of my meat with the sauce. It gives it more taste. All of the meat was very good. Chicken was surprisingly tender. All of the lamb and meatballs were great. I highly recommend this, it’s a bit of everything. -pistachio and cheese kunefe 4 - this is not a bad dessert. Compared to the other two we had, it was okay. -orange pistachio semolina with ice cream 4.5 - I would recommend getting this if you like orange. I like the ice cream in the middle. It is heavy to eat and filling. -pistachio cheesecake 5 - not very sweet at all. Very smooth. Probably one of the best desserts there. Food: 4 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 5 Recommended dishes CYO Mix Grill, Lahmacun 1pc, Pistachio Cheesecake, Cheesecake, Chicken Shish, Lamb Chops Loud, but you can still talk

reviews.name: Jose Tolentino
reviews.review_text: I've dined here twice for dinner this past February 2026, on the Tuesday nights when they serve Kokoreç! Absolutely DELICIOUS and authentic, just like the Kelle Paça and Cig Kofte! The food is flavorful, hearty and like nothing I've ever had in Illinois! Even their nearby competitor - A Thousand Tales - serves nothing like this food (which explains why I've usually been the only non-Turkish diner each time I've dined here!) My server both times was Karinna--she was very informative, pleasant and efficient (which is why I tipped her 50% each time)! The inside of the place is clean, cozy with interesting avocado green colored booths, and brightly lit, with lots of plants all over the place and relaxing Turkish music playing overhead! I will definitely be back!!! Food: 5 Service: 5 Atmosphere: 5 Reservations not required Would not recommend This is NOT the place for vegetarians — nowhere near as many options as an Indian restaurant!! Plenty of parking Free parking lot Saw families with kids here every time I’ve dined here; they all appeared to be happy with the food, service and ambience! Yes - wheelchair accessible (no stairs to worry about) but the aisles between tables and booths are not that wide. This place is not as spacious as their competitor, A Thousand Tales.
